rationale: The plan correctly matches a negative-binomial count model (DESeq2 Wald with apeglm shrinkage, cross-checked by edgeR QL F-test) to raw Salmon counts in an unpaired, single-batch, two-group design with n=3, keeps alpha at 0.05 rather than compensating, and states the power caveat explicitly; the edgeR intersection framing as a 'high-confidence set' is defensible but slightly non-standard and risks under-reporting DESeq2-only calls. QC is well specified (blind VST, PCA on top 500, distance heatmap, library sizes, explicit outlier-flagging policy), the filter (>=10 counts in >=3 samples, tied to the smallest group) is minimal and justified, and normalization is correctly internal (median-of-ratios / TMM) with no pre-normalized input. The design formula ~condition with an explicitly set 'control' reference and a named treated-vs-control contrast is correct and specific to this design; BH at a stated alpha with independent filtering and apeglm-shrunken LFCs reported alongside unshrunken values is exactly right. Enrichment is not strictly demanded by the question but is well constructed (full ranked list by Wald stat, tested-genes universe, named collections with versions, 15-500 size window, ORA correctly rejected) — deducted only because human gene sets and org.Hs.eg.db are assumed without any stated species verification for the liver samples. Reporting is complete: gene counts tested and significant, diagnostics, versions, seed, and honest design caveats.
